newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says coalition united on pensions.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says coalition united on pensions.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday his coalition was united about how to confront the thorny issue of pension reforms.

"There are absolutely no differences within the government on the issue of how to confront reform of the welfare state, which must in any case remain a means of defending the weakest," Prodi told a news conference.
Prodi said a commission studying social service spending would complete its work in a few weeks and that Italians would be asked their opinion of its conclusions.
Prodi said his coalition was in continuous dialogue over social spending with the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, on which it depends for a majority in the lower house of parliament.
He said he was certain there would be "points of convergence" with Communist Refoundation over social spending that would not conflict with the programme of his centre-left Olive Tree coalition.
Italy's generous pensions system is a highly politically sensitive issue. Communist Refoundation has vowed to bring down the government if social spending is cut.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in an interview on Monday that some adjustment to Italy's pensions spending was "probable" and as far as he was concerned, the soooner it happened the better.

Welfare state reform also has become a more pressing issue as Italy tries to bring its state finances into line in order to meet the economic criteria that will allow it to be among the founding members of European economic and monetary union (EMU). --Rome newsroom +396-678-2501
